Section cdc_child:006 (page 7) continues the COVID-19 vaccination notes for moderately or severely immunocompromised persons. No rules were produced because every recommendation depends on information the grammar cannot express: prior product received (Moderna, Pfizer-BioNTech, Novavax), number of prior doses, dose-to-dose intervals and product choice.

Not represented (continued from the prior page, apparently a younger immunocompromised age group): incomplete-series catch-up for prior Pfizer-BioNTech ('1 dose Pfizer-BioNTech: complete initial series with 2 doses 2024–25 Pfizer-BioNTech at least 4 weeks apart') and prior Novavax; and completed-series guidance ('2 doses 2024–25 Moderna or Novavax or Pfizer-BioNTech 6 months apart (minimum interval 2 months)') for people with 3 or more prior Moderna or Pfizer-BioNTech doses, or 2 or more prior Novavax doses.

Not represented, for 'Age 18 years who ARE moderately or severely immunocompromised': unvaccinated persons get 4 doses (Moderna or Pfizer-BioNTech 3-dose initial series plus 1 dose 6 months later) or 3 doses (Novavax 2-dose initial series plus 1 dose). Dose count depends on product choice, and the population's age bounds are unclear from this page alone.

Not represented: the same-manufacturer requirement for the initial series ('Use vaccine from the same manufacturer for all doses in the initial vaccination series'); minimum intervals (3 weeks, 4 weeks, 8 weeks, 2 months, 6 months); and incomplete- and complete-series catch-up logic for the age-18 group.

Not represented: 'moderately or severely immunocompromised' is narrower than the vocabulary concept 'immunocompromised'. It would need a new concept (e.g. moderate_severe_immunocompromise) defined by external CDC criteria, which are only linked here, not stated.
Not represented (uncomputable): additional doses are 'based on shared clinical decision-making and administered at least 2 months after the most recent dose'.

Informational only, not rules: no preferential recommendation among products; age-transition tables (age 4 to 5, 11 to 12) are referenced externally; references to interchangeability and EUA information.
